correctness.rationale: Spectrum of complete bipartite Laplacian has three nonzero values p,q,p+q (two when p=q); block square gives four necessary/sufficient positivity conditions beta>=0, alpha>=(p+q)beta, both holding diagonals nonnegative. Unconstrained equioscillating quadratic f has f(p)=f(p+q)=tau, f(q)=-tau with beta=2/[p(p+3q)] and alpha=(2p+q)beta. Weak sign changes of h(t)/t, an affine function, prove strict uniqueness. Its high-degree holding probability is nonnegative iff (p-2)q<=p². Above, alpha=(q+2p)/[q(2p-1)], beta=1/[q(2p-1)] saturate this diagonal; then f(p)=f(p+q)=((p-1)q-p²)/[q(2p-1)] and f(q)=-1/(2p-1). Perturbation u,v constrained u<=(q+1)v produces strict SLEM increase for any v sign, proving uniqueness. At p=q exact degree-two interpolation kills two positive modes. Two separately nonnegative Euler factors require 0<=gamma_i<=1/q and retain p-eigenvalue >=(1-p/q)², while quadratic rate tends (p-1)/(2p-1). Independently checked 78 integer instances with exact fractions and an LP formulation; universal result is analytic.
